newsitem.title: USA: US commissioner raises merger market power concern.
newsitem.headline: US commissioner raises merger market power concern.

text.p: U.S. energy regulator William Massey Monday apologized that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission had taken more than two years to decide on the Primergy merger, but stood by the FERC's rejection of the union as proposed because of market power concerns.

Wisconsin Energy Corp and Northern States Power Co called off their merger last week after the FERC decision, partly because they believed that any further delay in winning approval for their plan would trim its benefits.
"That merger had been before us for a number of months, ... and I'm sorry about that," FERC commissioner William Massey told a Washington International Energy Group gathering.
But he made no apology for the commission's decision, saying the FERC would not ignore questions about concentrating power generation assets in a few hands.
"FERC is not going to turn a blind eye to market power concerns," he said.
"There were serious market power concerns in this case," said Massey, who was not present for the commission's vote last week on the Primergy merger but endorsed its decision.
Massey is under consideration to replace Elizabeth Moler as chairman of the commission, assuming she is approved by the Senate to become the new deputy secretary of energy.
